To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HPR0 has low translational efficiency and that as HPR length increases the translational efficiency of the gene increases, which is correlated with mortality rates caused by ISA viruses.
the HPR of the ISA virus HE gene modifies the translational efficiency of the gene and that this effect is correlated with the virulence of different isolates of ISA viruses.
HPR of the ISA virus affects the efficiency of HE translation and that this efficiency correlates with virulence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the HPR on the translational efficiency of the HE gene and the relationship with the observed mortality caused by the ISA virus.
the role of codon-pairs in the evolution of the HPR of ISA viruses and their influence on the virulence of this pathogen.
the identification of a new mechanism that could explain the virulence of ISA virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HPR size of the HE gene of ISA viruses correlates with the virulence of these viruses.
HPR size correlates with virulence and this correlation is mediated by the translational efficiency of HE gene.
HPR size and codon-pair composition are correlated to virulence, which may be due to a decrease in translational efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HPR size of ISA virus HE genes correlates with the virulence of this virus, and this is related to the translational efficiency of the HE gene.

HPR0 is avirulent because the translational machinery of the host cannot efficiently translate the HE gene, while viruses with HPR of different lengths are virulent due to the translational machinery adaptation to the HE gene, which is reflected in the mortality rate caused by the virus.
the HPR region of the HE gene has an important role in ISA virus pathogenicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HPR of ISA virus is involved in the adaptation of the virus to the host and that the HPR size is correlated with mortality rates caused by this virus.
the HE protein, which is not essential for viral replication but is important for virulence, could be a target for the design of attenuated ISA vaccines.
the use of codons in pairs is important to the virulence of ISA virus and that this use can be manipulated to control the virulence of this virus.
